description:
Source: _project/audits/results-explorer-publication-adversarial-review.md
(develop_sha fddedf26), findings §2.20 (Advisory) and §2.21 (Advisory).

§2.20 — The publisher's canonical set is
benchbox/core/publishing/bundle_publisher.py:30
VALID_LABELS = (maintainer-run, community-submission, ci, local,
unofficial-research). But the explorer's TrustBadge config keys are
ci-verified, ci-validated, local-run
(results-explorer/src/components/TrustBadge.tsx:19-43) and ranking
eligibility is {maintainer-run, ci-verified} (models.py:82-89). So a bundle
labeled `ci` or `local` by the publisher renders under the "unrecognised —
contact maintainers" fallback and (for `ci`) is not ranking-eligible despite
the publisher treating it as first-class; `unofficial-research` has no
explorer badge at all. The two halves of the platform disagree on the label
vocabulary.

§2.21 — TrustBadge.tsx:64 `if (!trustLabel) return null;` hides the badge
entirely on an empty label instead of showing an explicit "unknown" (moot
today because the snapshot schema makes trust_label NOT NULL, but the
component contract is hide-on-missing).

anti_patterns.dont: add a third divergent label set
anti_patterns.instead: collapse to one canonical vocabulary referenced by both sides.

preserves.behavior: Existing curated badge tones for maintainer-run and ci-verified.
is_ranking_eligible semantics: community-submission and local stay excluded from official rankings.

prior_art.concept: benchbox/core/publishing/bundle_publisher.py:30 VALID_LABELS — reuse as (or reconcile toward) the canonical vocabulary.
results-explorer/src/components/TrustBadge.tsx:TRUST_CONFIG — extend to cover every canonical label.
results-explorer/src/lib/displayLabels.ts:formatTrustLabel — reuse the existing 'unknown' rendering for the empty-state fix.

verifications.description: Every publisher VALID_LABELS value renders a non-fallback badge; empty renders 'unknown'
verifications.expected: new/updated test asserts each VALID_LABELS value maps to a curated badge (not the 'unrecognised' fallback) and empty → 'unknown'; suite passes

verifications.description: The ci↔ci-verified / local↔local-run mappings are covered by a test, not just a grep
verifications.expected: a test enumerates the canonical labels and asserts each resolves; fails if a VALID_LABELS value is unmapped

work_units.notes:
Pick the single source of truth (publisher VALID_LABELS vs explorer
TRUST_CONFIG) and reconcile ci↔ci-verified and local↔local-run
explicitly. Ensure unofficial-research has an explorer badge. Document the
canonical list where both sides reference it.

2026-07-06 FOLLOW-UP FIX (review-followup-sweep): the ci↔ci-verified
reconciliation only landed on the explorer badge side (TrustBadge.tsx
got a distinct `ci` entry alongside `ci-verified`) -- the ranking side
was missed. `bundle_publisher.VALID_LABELS` has never accepted
"ci-verified" as a label (it's parametrized as a bad/invalid case in
test_bundle_publisher_label.py); the publisher's real spelling is "ci".
But `RANKING_ELIGIBLE_TRUST_LABELS` in
`_project/scripts/explorer_pipeline/models.py` only listed
"ci-verified", so every bundle the publisher could actually produce
with the ci label was structurally excluded from official rankings --
the exact §2.20 defect this TODO was opened to close, still live.
Fixed by adding "ci" to RANKING_ELIGIBLE_TRUST_LABELS (kept
"ci-verified" too, since TrustBadge.tsx still renders it distinctly for
any historical data using that spelling). Added
test_ci_public_verified_is_eligible and extended
test_ranking_eligible_trust_labels_constant.
work_units.summary: Define one canonical trust-label vocabulary shared by the publisher, pipeline, and explorer

work_units.notes:
Update results-explorer/src/components/TrustBadge.tsx TRUST_CONFIG so
every VALID_LABELS value renders a curated badge; keep the fallback only
for genuinely unknown strings.
work_units.summary: Map every publisher label to an explorer badge (no silent 'unrecognised' for a valid label)

work_units.notes:
TrustBadge.tsx:64 — render DEFAULT_CONFIG/'unknown' on empty rather than
hiding the trust dimension. Update the pinning tests
(results-explorer/src/components/__tests__/).
work_units.summary: Render an explicit 'unknown' badge on empty trust label instead of returning null
